edits.before: In our positive left-over-right convention, increasing top-vertex order makes them descending: a pair that crosses once has its initially left strand still on the left just before that crossing, so that strand crosses over.
edits.after: In the positive right-over-left convention, these permutation braids are descending for the auxiliary traversal in decreasing top-vertex order: a pair that crosses once has its initially right strand still on the right just before that unique crossing, so that strand crosses over and is traversed first. This auxiliary traversal is not the increasing-initial-endpoint traversal defining the standard matching basis in the Statement; the positive permutation lifts need not be those standard basis representatives. Their use below requires their braid-word identities and distinct connectors, for which step 4.1 permits arbitrary representatives.
